Flag wells whose blank-corrected signal never rises

flag_no_growth.Rd

A well is flagged when its blank-corrected OD never climbs more than min_rise above its starting level, where the starting level is the mean of its first n_reads reads. Wells with a flat curve (for example wells with no inoculum) are flagged. The threshold is a judgement call that depends on your instrument noise and culture density, so check it against known growing and non-growing wells.

Usage

flag_no_growth(data, min_rise = 0.05, n_reads = 5, od = "od_corrected")

Arguments

data

Data frame with blank-corrected OD, from blank_correct().

min_rise

Smallest rise in OD (maximum minus starting level) for a well to count as growing.

n_reads

Number of initial reads averaged to get the starting level.

od

Name of the blank-corrected OD column.

Value

data with added well-level logical column flag_no_growth. It is NA for wells with no readings (for example unused wells).

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "bioscreen_example.txt", package = "plateReadeR")
d <- flag_no_growth(blank_correct(read_bioscreen(f)))
unique(d[c("plate_id", "well", "flag_no_growth")])
#> # A tibble: 200 × 3
#>    plate_id well  flag_no_growth
#>    <chr>    <chr> <lgl>         
#>  1 Plate 1  001   TRUE          
#>  2 Plate 1  002   TRUE          
#>  3 Plate 1  003   TRUE          
#>  4 Plate 1  004   TRUE          
#>  5 Plate 1  005   TRUE          
#>  6 Plate 1  006   TRUE          
#>  7 Plate 1  007   TRUE          
#>  8 Plate 1  008   TRUE
